cards.objective: Explain the thickness of the left ventricular wall.
cards.front: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than the right’s?
cards.answer: It pumps against the systemic circuit’s resistance

why.t: The left ventricle’s wall is much thicker than the right’s, to pump against the higher resistance of the systemic circuit. The right side of the heart feeds the pulmonary circuit; the left side feeds the systemic circuit.

simpler.t: The heart is a pump about the size of your fist. It pushes blood all round your body.

depth.t: Ventricles: the two lower chambers, the main pumps: right to the lungs, left to the body.
Valves: tricuspid and mitral between atria and ventricles; pulmonary and aortic at the exits.
Septa: walls between the chambers: interatrial, interventricular and atrioventricular.
Myocardium: the thick middle layer of the wall, made of cardiac muscle that pumps the blood.

clinical.t: A coronary artery blocked by atherosclerotic plaque. Without blood and oxygen, the cardiac muscle cells die.

trap.t: Both ventricles pump the same volume per beat; the left must generate more pressure.

cards.source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 19.1 Heart Anatomy; 19.5 Development of the Heart
